newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Corimon oks share conversion, ADRs to resume trade.
newsitem.headline: Corimon oks share conversion, ADRs to resume trade.

text.p: Venezuelan paints and packaging company Corimon agreed late Monday to convert its preferred B shares to A shares at the rate of 10:13.5, the company said.
"This will enable Corimon's American Depository Receipts (ADRs) to return to trading on the New York Stock Exchange as of Monday, July 28," the company said in a press release.

The company's B shares are the result of debt/equity swap with creditors, used to bail out the company when it was brought down last year by its money-loosing California subsidiary Standard Brand Paints.
Trading on both the NYSE and Caracas bolsa's was suspended in February 1996. Local trade re-opened October 1996.

In the company's annual general meeting late Monday, shareholders also approved a capital increase of up to 4.3 billion bolivars ($8.7 million) through the issue of up to 427 million B shares at a nominal value of 10 bolivars.
The stock closed Monday at 20.00 bolivars. A-issue shares meanwhile closed at 16.80 bolivars.
"This will take the company's paid-in equity to 56.8 billion bolivars," Corimon said.

Analysts credit the company with emerging relatively quickly from a vast and painful restructuring process that saw creditors, holding debts totaling $100.8 million, take control of over 80 percent of the company's equity last year.
